Crews and customer support teams worked through the holiday in wind gusts up to 70 mph and heavy rain and continue restoration efforts across the Mid-Atlantic region.

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Exelon and its operating companies mobilized employees, contractors and mutual-assistance resources during Thanksgiving as a powerful nor’easter brought damaging winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding to parts of the Mid-Atlantic, causing widespread damage and power outages.

The storm swept across the Mid-Atlantic, leaving hundreds of thousands of customers without service across BGE, PECO, Atlantic City Electric, Delmarva Power and Pepco territories. As of early Friday afternoon, the vast majority of those outages had been restored quickly and safely. Exelon continues to direct additional resources to the areas with the most severe damage to restore power to customers still without service.

"Our customers count on us every day, and that responsibility takes on a special meaning during the holidays, when families are gathering and communities are depending on us," said Mike Innocenzo, Exelon’s Chief Operating Officer. "Thousands of Exelon employees, contractors and partners have answered the call this holiday to safely restore power in the communities where they live and work. I want to thank them for being there for our customers and their neighbors when it matters most, and for staying on until the work is done."

Working around the clock for customers and their families

Across the Mid-Atlantic, crews from BGE, PECO, Atlantic City Electric, Delmarva Power and Pepco continue to work around the clock to restore power quickly and safely in some of the storm’s harshest conditions. Coastal wind gusts reached speeds as high as 70 mph in parts of New Jersey, Delaware and Maryland, while several inches of rain and flooding brought down trees, limbs, poles and wires and closed roads, limiting safe access to some of the hardest-hit areas. Exelon is moving resources to where they are needed most, including ComEd mutual assistance personnel and resources from the Chicagoland area that have traveled east to reinforce the hardest-hit communities.

Always on, with safety first

Throughout our service territories, dedicated employees work around the clock, preparing before storms, responding when conditions are at their worst and staying on the job until every customer is restored. Safety remains our top priority. Exelon and its utilities urge customers to stay away from downed wires and always assume they are energized. Customers should report outages and check their local utility's website or mobile app for the latest restoration information.

About Exelon

Exelon (Nasdaq: EXC) is a Fortune 200 company and one of the nation’s largest utility companies, serving almost 11 million customers through six fully regulated transmission and distribution utilities — Atlantic City Electric, BGE, ComEd, Delmarva Power, PECO, and Pepco. Exelon’s more than 20,000 employees dedicate their time and expertise to supporting our communities through reliable, affordable and efficient energy delivery, workforce development, equity, economic development and volunteerism. MALVERN, Pa., Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Annovis Bio, Inc. (NYSE: ANVS) (“Annovis” or the “Company”), a Phase 3 clinical-stage biotechnology company developing buntanetap, an investigational once-daily pill for neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD), today announced that on November 25, 2026, it received written notice from the New York Stock Exchange (the "NYSE"). The notice states that the Company is not in compliance with Section 802.01C of the NYSE Listed Company Manual. That section requires the average closing price of a listed company's common stock to be at least $1.00 per share over a consecutive 30 trading-day period. As of November 24, 2026, the 30 trading-day average closing price of the Company's common stock was $0.93.

The Company has six months after receiving the notice to regain compliance with the minimum share price requirement. During that time, the Company's common stock will continue to be listed and traded on the NYSE under the symbol "ANVS," with a ".BC" indicator showing that the Company is below the NYSE's continued listing standards. The Company will regain compliance if on the last trading day of any calendar month during the cure period its closing share price is at least $1.00 and its average closing share price over the 30 trading days ending that day is also at least $1.00.

The Company intends to notify the NYSE within the required 10 business days of its intent to cure the deficiency. The Company intends to monitor the closing price of its common stock and to consider all available options to regain compliance, which may include a reverse stock split, subject to stockholder approval.

As previously disclosed, on October 29, 2026, the Company received a separate notice from the NYSE because its average global market capitalization over a consecutive 30 trading-day period was below $50 million and, at the same time, its stockholders' equity was below $50 million. The Company remains subject to the conditions in that notice. The cure periods under the two standards run independently of each other.

The NYSE notice does not immediately affect the listing or trading of the Company's common stock. The notice also does not affect the Company's business operations or its reporting obligations with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and it does not conflict with or cause an event of default under any of the Company's material debt or other agreements.

About Annovis
Headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, Annovis Bio, Inc. (NYSE: ANVS) is a Phase 3 clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). The Company's lead drug candidate, buntanetap (formerly posiphen), is an investigational once-daily oral therapy that inhibits the translation of multiple neurotoxic proteins, including APP and amyloid beta, tau, alpha-synuclein, and TDP-43, through a specific RNA-targeting mechanism of action. By addressing the underlying causes of neurodegeneration, Annovis aims to halt disease progression and improve cognitive and motor functions in patients. For more information, visit www.annovisbio.com and follow us on LinkedIn, YouTube, and X.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phaos Technology Holdings (Cayman) Limited (NYSE American: POAS) ("Phaos" or the "Company") today outlined an opportunity to develop automated car wash and vehicle care services in Southeast Asia, particularly in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. The Company is evaluating Singapore and Malaysia as initial markets for services that combine convenience for drivers and fleet operators with automation and water reuse. In a second phase, it may consider expanding into other Southeast Asian markets.

Singapore had more than 650,000 cars in October 2026, including nearly 99,000 private-hire cars, according to Land Transport Authority data1. In Malaysia, the Malaysian Automotive Association2 reported 630,461 new passenger vehicles sold from January through October 2026, up about 4% year over year. Separately, Grand View Research3 estimates that Malaysia's broader car wash services market could grow from US$208.9 million in 2025 to US$361.7 million by 2033, a projected annual growth rate of 7.3% from 2026 to 2033. The forecast covers multiple wash formats and does not estimate revenue for Phaos.

In Indonesia, Ken Research4 estimates that paid professional car wash services could grow from US$390 million in 2025 to US$686 million in 2032, or 8.4% annually. In Thailand, a nationwide National Statistical Office survey5 put 2023 receipts for businesses classified under car washing, polishing and similar services at THB 14.1 billion. In October 2026, Bangchak6 reported Lodon JetX automated washes at 50 of its fuel stations, showing adoption of the format. The two market figures cover broader service categories and do not measure Phaos's addressable revenue.

Phaos is exploring the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to automate car washing, with the aim of reducing labor costs and improving water recycling. In Singapore, Inchcape reported that the automated gantry it developed with Kärcher can recycle up to 85% of the water used per wash.7

"We see an opportunity to serve vehicles that need regular care," said Gan Hong Loon, Chief Executive Officer of Phaos. "Singapore and specific regions in Malaysia give us places to test demand and site economics before we consider expanding."

Headquartered in Singapore, Phaos has its roots in advanced microscopy and is pursuing a strategic repositioning toward engineering, procurement and construction (EPC). For more information, visit the company website.8

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Mundoro Capital Inc. (TSXV: MUN ) (OTCQB: MUNMF) (www.mundoro.com) ("Mundoro" or the "Company") announces the filing of its condensed interim consolidated financial statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, together with a series of changes to its finance, audit and board structure designed to optimize the allocation of the Company's capital to its project portfolio.

Highlights

  • Q3 2026 results filed: corporate expenses of $1,002,990 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of 3% compared with the same period in 2025. Cash of $2,962,438 as at September 30, 2026 and no long-term debt.

  • New Chief Financial Officer: Anil Jiwani returns to Mundoro as CFO effective December 1, 2026, succeeding James (Jim) Scott.

  • Change of auditor: Davidson & Company LLP appointed as the Company's auditor, replacing PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP. The change was initiated by the Company following a competitive proposal process.

  • Streamlined Board: the Board of Directors will be reduced from five to four directors effective December 31, 2026, three of whom are independent.

  • Strategic investment closed: The private placement by Centerra Gold Inc., previously announced on November 6, 2026, closed on November 27, 2026.

Teo Dechev, CEO, President and Director of Mundoro, stated, "In Serbia, our partner-funded exploration programs completed 4,363 metres of drilling, new AMT and gravity surveys and the re-logging of more than 20,000 metres of drilled core from various drilling campaigns over the last 10 years, advancing seven porphyry targets, five of them with drill proposals in place. We added two new senior members to our technical and operations teams, and we restructured our accounting and administration functions to optimize the use of our capital in advancing our portfolio. We also welcomed Centerra Gold as a new strategic shareholder through a private placement. We will seek new partners to advance the drill-ready targets on the eight licences in Serbia returning to 100% Mundoro ownership. Mundoro enters 2027 with funding in place, a more efficient cost structure and a clear focus on advancing opportunities across our portfolio."

Capital Efficiency and Corporate Structure

Mundoro reviews its cost structure every year with the aim of directing a greater share of its capital toward its project pipeline. In 2026, the review focused on the administration side of the business: finance, audit, governance and corporate support. The changes announced today are the outcome of that review and are designed to restructure fixed corporate costs while maintaining the quality of the Company's financial reporting and oversight. The Company also continually looks for ways to improve its workflows and efficiency across the organization.

The finance function moves to a model in which the CFO role is provided through an external firm, giving the Company access to a broader team of accounting professionals without the fixed cost of a larger in-house team. The change of auditor aligns the audit with the Company's generator business model, and a four-member Board, sized to the Company's current stage, optimizes governance costs while maintaining a majority of independent directors.

Appointment of Chief Financial Officer

Mundoro announces the appointment of Anil Jiwani, CPA, CA, as Chief Financial Officer, effective December 1, 2026. Mr. Jiwani previously served as CFO of Mundoro from 2017 to 2018 and brings a working knowledge of the Company's financial structure, partner arrangements and projects. His services will be provided through Avisar Everyday Solutions Ltd. ("Avisar"), which gives the Company access to a broader team of accounting professionals. Mr. Jiwani has more than 20 years of experience in accounting, corporate finance and public company reporting, primarily in the mining and mineral exploration sector. He is also Chief Operating Officer and a director of Avisar.

Mr. Jiwani succeeds James (Jim) Scott, who has served as CFO since July 2026, and previously from June 2022 to January 2025, and who oversaw the preparation of the Company's third quarter 2026 filings. The Board and management thank Jim for his service and contributions to the Company's financial reporting and wish him well in his future endeavours.

Change of Auditor

The Company has changed its auditor from PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP ("PwC") to Davidson & Company LLP ("Davidson"). The change was initiated by the Company following a request-for-proposal process overseen by the Audit Committee, and was not the result of a resignation by PwC. Davidson was selected for its experience with mineral exploration, generator and royalty companies, and for a cost-effective fee structure. There were no modified opinions in PwC's reports on the Company's financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, and there have been no "reportable events", as defined in National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations ("NI 51-102"). In accordance with NI 51-102, the Notice of Change of Auditor, together with the letters from PwC and Davidson, has been reviewed and approved by the Audit Committee and the Board and filed on SEDAR+. The Company thanks PwC for its services over the last 13 years.

Change in Board Composition

As part of the organizational review and capital efficiency initiatives, the Board will be reduced from five to four directors. In connection with this reduction, Stephen Altmann will step down from the Board effective December 31, 2026. The Board and management thank Mr. Altmann for his contributions to Mundoro over the past five years and wish Stephen continued success in his future endeavours. The Board will comprise three independent directors and one non-independent director. Michael Calyniuk serves as Lead Director and will assume the role of Chair of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Siegfried Weidner will assume the role of Chair of the Compensation Committee. Mark Platt continues to serve as Chair of the Audit Committee.

Q3 2026 Financial Highlights

For complete details of the Company's financial results, please refer to the condensed interim consolidated financial statements and MD&A for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The Company's filings are available on SEDAR+ and on Mundoro's website at www.mundoro.com under the heading Investors. All amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars unless otherwise indicated.

Fees Earned: The Company's fee income, which includes operator fees, option payments, interest, and miscellaneous income, totaled $287,039 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to $246,566 for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $40,473. The increase was driven by higher operator fee income recognized during Q3 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

Exploration Expenditures: Exploration expenditures, represent both sole funded exploration by partners and expenditures for generative activities for the Company, together those were $2,767,738 in Q3 2026 compared to $1,710,067 in Q3 2025, representing an increase of $1,057,671. Recoveries from option partners in Q3 2026 were $2,701,888 compared to $1,354,720 in Q3 2025.

Generative Activities: Generative activities create long-term royalty opportunities and may generate future property payments, milestone payments, and other fees through the optioning of mineral projects to third parties. Included in total exploration expenditures are net exploration costs attributable to the Company's generative operations in the three jurisdictions where it is active and which are funded by the Company. These expenditures resulted in $65,850 in Q3 2026 compared to $355,347 in Q3 2025.

Corporate Expenses: Corporate expenses in Q3 2026 were $379,897 compared to $369,862 in Q3 2025, representing an increase of $10,035.

Cash and Working Capital: As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents totaling $2,962,438 (December 31, 2025 - $5,217,157) and a working capital (current assets less current liabilities) of $1,064,255 (December 31, 2025 - $1,684,464). This cash balance includes $1,530,801 of net advances from partners, which is required to be used on exploration activities.

Net Income (Loss): For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a net loss of $269,840 ($0.00 per share) compared to a net loss of $412,352 ($0.00 per share) for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, representing a decrease in net loss of $142,511.

SCOTTSDALE, AZ / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Southwest Heritage Bank, together with the bank's parent company, Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTCID:BCTF), today announced a definitive agreement for Peak Credit Union ("Peak") to acquire Southwest Heritage Bank. Under the agreement, Peak would acquire substantially all of Southwest Heritage Bank's assets and assume substantially all of its liabilities in an all-cash transaction.

The transaction was unanimously approved by the boards of directors of Peak Credit Union, Southwest Heritage Bank, and Bancorp 34, Inc. The acquisition is subject to customary regulatory and stockholder approvals and is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027. Following completion of the transaction, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. will dissolve and the remaining assets will be distributed to the stockholders of Bancorp 34, Inc. Subject to the terms of the agreement, stockholders are expected to receive an estimated $20.67 to $22.18 per share for an aggregate transaction value of $ 159 million to $171 million.

Peak intends to retain members of Southwest Heritage Bank's executive leadership team in senior roles within the combined organization, drawing on their expertise and experience to guide a successful integration and contribute to the credit union's long-term growth and strategic direction. In particular, Southwest Heritage Bank President Paul Tees will be responsible for leading commercial banking across the combined organization, bringing the bank's commercial lending expertise and local-market-led, relationship focused approach to Peak's broader network.

Peak also intends to retain all Southwest Heritage Bank employees immediately upon closing, subject to ordinary business and individual circumstances, to ensure continuity of service and the successful integration of the organizations' systems and processes.

Until the transaction closes, both organizations will continue to operate independently, and there is nothing customers or members need to do.

D.A. Davidson & Co. served as financial advisor and Otteson Shapiro LLP served as legal counsel to Bancorp 34, Inc. and Southwest Heritage Bank. McQueen Financial Advisors served as financial advisor and Luse Gorman, PC served as legal counsel to Peak Credit Union.

Winnipeg, Manitoba--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. (NASDAQ: FNUC) ("Frontier"), a nuclear fuel cycle company, announces that on November 25, 2026, it received a written notification letter (the "Notification Letter") from the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq"), notifying Frontier that it was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as the minimum bid price of Frontier's common shares ("Shares") has been below US $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification Letter is only a notification of deficiency and not a notice of delisting. As such, the Notification Letter has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of Frontier's Shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "FNUC."

Nasdaq Listing Rules

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires securities listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share, and Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. Based on the closing bid price of Frontier's Shares for the 30 consecutive business days from October 14, 2026 to November 24, 2026, Frontier has not met the minimum bid price requirement.

In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), Frontier has a period of 180 calendar days, or until May 24, 2027 in which to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Frontier's Shares must meet or exceed US $1.00 for at least ten consecutive business days during this 180-calendar day period. In the event Frontier does not regain compliance by May 24, 2027, Frontier may be eligible for an additional 180 calendar day grace period if it meets the continued listing requirement for market value of publicly held shares (US $1 million) and all other initial listing standards for The Nasdaq Capital Market, with the exception of the bid price and provides written notice to Nasdaq of its intention to cure the deficiency during the second compliance period, by effecting a reverse stock split, if necessary. If it appears to Nasdaq that Frontier will not be able to cure the deficiency, or if Frontier is not otherwise eligible for additional time to regain compliance, Frontier's Shares will be subject to delisting by Nasdaq. Frontier may still appeal Nasdaq's determination to delist its Shares, and during any appeal process, Frontier's Shares would continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

Frontier is issuing this press release pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(b). Nasdaq advised Frontier that it will be added to Nasdaq's public list of non-compliant companies beginning five business days after the date of the notice. Nasdaq will also distribute a non-compliance indicator through its market data network and make it available to third-party market data providers.

Frontier's management intends to actively monitor the bid price for its Shares and will consider all available options to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement.

Frontier's business operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter.

The proposed acquisition would deepen business banking expertise and expand Peak's reach into Arizona and New Mexico

EUGENE, Ore. and LACEY, Wash. and SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak Credit Union announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all assets and assume all liabilities of Southwest Heritage Bank, a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTC: BCTF), in an all-cash transaction.

The proposed acquisition would bring together Peak's broad consumer financial services and member-owned cooperative model with Southwest Heritage's commercial lending expertise, treasury management services, and established business relationships across Arizona and New Mexico. The combination is intended to expand the financial resources available to individuals and business owners while preserving the local expertise and personal relationships valued by Southwest Heritage customers.

"Our focus is on finding meaningful ways to serve more people," said Dr. David L. Tuyo II, president and CEO of Peak Credit Union. "We know many of our members already spend part of the year in Arizona, making it a natural place for us to grow. Southwest Heritage has built trusted relationships with local businesses, backed by people who understand their communities. Bringing that expertise together with Peak's broader capabilities gives us an opportunity to help more people and businesses move toward their financial goals."

Over time, Peak members could benefit from deeper commercial lending and treasury management capabilities, while Southwest Heritage customers could gain access to additional consumer financial services. Specific products, eligibility, and timing will be determined as integration planning progresses.

The employees and relationships of Southwest Heritage Bank are central to the value of the planned transition. Peak intends to retain Southwest Heritage employees at closing, subject to ordinary business and individual circumstances, to support service continuity and integration. Peak also intends to retain members of Southwest Heritage's executive leadership team in senior roles. Final roles and reporting relationships remain subject to approval and integration planning.

There are no immediate changes to branch operations, accounts, or banking services as a result of today's announcement. Until the transaction closes, the two organizations are expected to continue to operate independently, and members and customers do not need to take any action. It is expected that Peak will communicate any future changes directly and in advance.

The boards of directors of Peak Credit Union, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. approved the agreement unanimously. The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals and is expected to close in the second half of 2027.

Following closing, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. is expected to dissolve and distribute the remaining assets of Bancorp 34, Inc. to its shareholders in accordance with the transaction terms.

D.A. Davidson & Co. served as financial advisor and Otteson Shapiro LLP served as legal counsel to Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. McQueen Financial Advisors served as financial advisor and Luse Gorman, PC served as legal counsel to Peak Credit Union.

About Peak Credit Union: Peak Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative serving more than 250,000 members through 35 branches across Washington and Oregon and digital banking services. Formed from the combination of TwinStar Credit Union and Northwest Community Credit Union, Peak brings a longstanding commitment to financial education, accessible financial services and community well-being. Through the PeakCU Foundation, Peak supports local initiatives including classroom grants, scholarships and financial education. Federally insured by NCUA. Equal Housing Opportunity. Learn more at peakcu.org.

About Southwest Heritage Bank: Southwest Heritage Bank, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a community-focused bank serving individuals and businesses in Arizona and New Mexico. The bank offers commercial lending, treasury management and personal financial services, with an emphasis on local relationships and responsive service. Southwest Heritage Bank is a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTC: BCTF). Member FDIC. Learn more at swhbank.com.

The existing distribution reinvestment plan will be terminated as part of the Simplification with a similar plan for BEP Inc. to be established concurrently

BROOKFIELD, NEWS, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P. (“BEP”) (NYSE: BEP; TSX: BEP.UN) today announced updates to the plan of arrangement to advance the proposed corporate simplification (the “Simplification”) and declared its quarterly distribution.

In light of the expected benefits of the Simplification to all unitholders and approximately 62% of units voted to date with 99.7% of votes cast in favour, the BEP limited partnership agreement (“LPA”) and plan of arrangement were amended to facilitate completion of the Simplification. 

The amended plan of arrangement now requires approval by two-thirds of votes cast by Unitholders rather than approval by holders of two-thirds of all eligible units. Unitholders will no longer be required to vote on amendments to the BEP LPA and all other substantive terms of the plan of arrangement, including the tax implications and expected benefits for investors, have been retained.

Unitholders who have already submitted a proxy or voting instruction form do not need to vote again.

The deadline for registered unitholders to cast their votes by proxy will now be 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on December 7, 2026 with the Unitholders’ Meeting being held virtually on December 9, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. (Toronto time).

The quarterly distribution for BEP will be paid on December 21, 2026 to holders of record at the close of business on December 8, 2026, and it is expected that the Simplification will be completed by the end of 2026.

Corporate Simplification Details

Following an amendment to the BEP limited partnership agreement, the Simplification will now be completed pursuant to the terms of an amended plan of arrangement (the “Arrangement”). Upon receipt of approval from BEP unitholders of the Simplification, all outstanding limited partnership units of BEP, other than preferred units, will, together with certain related exchangeable securities, be exchanged on a one-for-one basis for newly issued shares of Brookfield Renewable Partners Inc. (“BEP Inc.”).

Shareholders of Brookfield Renewable Corporation (“BEPC”) have already approved the Simplification, pursuant to which their class A exchangeable subordinate voting shares will be exchanged for new shares of BEP Inc. on a one-for-one basis.

Benefits of a Simplified Structure

Brookfield Renewable expects the Simplification to be tax-deferred for Canadian and U.S. investors and completed without any meaningful cost to the business, while providing securityholders with the following benefits, among others:

  • Improved consolidated trading liquidity through a single listed security;
  • Increased demand from current indices and potential additional index inclusion;
  • Stronger alignment with long-term capital allocation trends toward indexable and ETF-eligible corporate securities;
  • Simplified investor analysis, screening, and benchmarking through a single listed reporting entity;
  • Broader access to a larger pool of investors who prefer corporate structures;
  • Enhanced governance framework and voting rights for public securityholders; and
  • For BEP unitholders, elimination of onerous partnership tax reporting forms and preferential dividend tax rates for many Canadian and U.S. taxable investors.

The Simplification will be implemented by way of a court-approved plan of arrangement and will be subject to customary regulatory approvals for a transaction of this nature, including approval for the listing of BEP Inc.’s shares on the New York Stock Exchange and Toronto Stock Exchange.

There will be no change to Brookfield’s ownership of Brookfield Renewable as a result of the Simplification. BEP’s preferred units and public debt will remain outstanding and unaffected by the Simplification.

The Board of Directors of BEP, based in part on the unanimous recommendation of its nominating and governance committee (consisting entirely of independent directors) and the fairness opinion previously received from Scotiabank, unanimously affirmed the conclusion that the Simplification, as amended, is in the best interests of BEP, and have unanimously resolved to approve the Simplification and recommend that BEP unitholders vote in favour of the Simplification.

Torys LLP is acting as legal advisor to Brookfield Renewable for the Simplification.

Scotiabank is acting as independent financial advisor, and Goodmans LLP is acting as independent legal counsel to the nominating and governance committees of each of BEP and BEPC in connection with the Simplification.

Further information regarding the Simplification, including details on the vote that will be required, will be contained in a disclosure supplement that will be available later today. Copies of the supplement, the arrangement agreement amendment, the amended plan of arrangement and certain related documents will be filed with the applicable Canadian securities regulators and with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission and will be available on SEDAR+ at https://sedarplus.ca and on EDGAR at https://sec.gov.

BEP Unitholders Who Have Questions or Require Voting Assistance

Brookfield Renewable has retained Laurel Hill Advisory Group (“Laurel Hill”) as its proxy solicitation agent. If you have any questions about the Unitholders’ Meeting or require assistance voting, please contact Laurel Hill:

Toll Free: 1-877-452-7184 (toll free in North America)
International: 1-416-304-0211
Text: text “INFO” to either number above
Email: assistance@laurelhill.com

Brookfield Renewable may also use the services of Broadridge Investor Communications to assist eligible beneficial unitholders with voting their units over the telephone with Laurel Hill. Many unitholders are eligible to vote quickly and easily over the phone, via email, or text message to help achieve the Simplification.

Please note that BEP has applied for exemptive relief from the Ontario Securities Commission in order to not require further approval by the holders of class A shares of Brookfield Renewable Partners Inc. (“BEP Inc. Class A Shares”) for any future distributions of BEP Inc. Class A Shares or securities that are, directly or indirectly, convertible into, or exercisable or exchangeable for, BEP Inc. Class A Shares under a prospectus, conditional upon obtaining the required securityholder approvals described in the joint management information circular (as supplemented). Accordingly, (i) in respect of BEPC, a vote in favour of the Simplification by BEPC shareholders constituted a vote in favour of BEP Inc.’s ability to conduct future issuances of BEP Inc. Class A Shares or securities that are, directly or indirectly, convertible into, or exercisable or exchangeable for, BEP Inc. Class A Shares pursuant to a prospectus, and (ii) in respect of BEP, a vote in favour of the Simplification by BEP unitholders will constitute a vote in favour of BEP Inc.’s ability to conduct future issuances of BEP Inc. Class A Shares or securities that are, directly or indirectly, convertible into, or exercisable or exchangeable for, BEP Inc. Class A Shares pursuant to a prospectus, in each case, without requiring further approval by holders of BEP Inc. Class A Shares in accordance with National Instrument 41-101 – General Prospectus Requirements.

Distribution Declaration and Update on Distribution Reinvestment Plan

The Q4 2026 quarterly distribution by BEP in the amount of $0.392 per LP unit will be payable on December 21, 2026 to unitholders of record as at the close of business on December 8, 2026. In conjunction with BEP’s distribution declaration, the Board of Directors of BEPC has declared an equivalent dividend of $0.392 per BEPC share, also payable on December 21, 2026 to shareholders of record as at the close of business on December 8, 2026. It is expected that the Simplification will be completed in December 2026, following the payment of distributions and dividends on December 21, 2026.

As a result of the expected timing of completion of the Simplification, BEP’s distribution reinvestment plan will be terminated effective November 27, 2026. The final distribution of BEP units under the plan was made in respect of BEP’s distribution paid on September 29, 2026 to unitholders of record as of August 31, 2026. Participants will receive the December 21, 2026 distribution in cash.

BEP Inc. expects to adopt a dividend reinvestment plan for the BEP Inc. Class A Shares that is substantially similar to BEP’s plan. Registered unitholders who currently participate in BEP’s distribution reinvestment plan will be required to confirm their enrolment in the BEP Inc. plan by June 21, 2027, and non-registered holders should contact their broker or other intermediary.

About Brookfield Renewable

Brookfield Renewable operates one of the world’s largest publicly traded platforms for renewable power and sustainable solutions. Our renewable power portfolio consists of hydroelectric, wind, utility-scale solar, distributed solar and storage facilities and our sustainable solutions assets include our investment in a leading global nuclear services business and a portfolio of investments in carbon capture and storage capacity, agricultural renewable natural gas, materials recycling and eFuels manufacturing capacity, among others.

Investors can access the portfolio either through Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P. (NYSE: BEP; TSX: BEP.UN), a Bermuda-based limited partnership, or Brookfield Renewable Corporation (NYSE, TSX: BEPC), a Canadian corporation. Further information is available at https://bep.brookfield.com.

Brookfield Renewable is the flagship listed energy company of Brookfield Asset Management, a global alternative asset manager, headquartered in New York with over $1 trillion of assets under management. For more information, go to https://brookfield.com.

Ottawa, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - C-COM Satellite Systems Inc., (TSXV: CMI) (OTCQB: CYSNF) a leading global provider of commercial grade mobile auto-deploying satellite antenna systems, announced today that, pursuant to the requirements of the TSX Venture Exchange, it has granted options to purchase 40,000 common shares of C-COM to an officer of C-COM. The stock options were granted pursuant to the terms of C-COM's stock option plan and are exercisable at $0.78 per share, being the closing price for the common shares on the TSX Venture Exchange on November 26, 2026. These grants form part of the overall annual remuneration package. Stock option grants are subject to necessary regulatory approvals.

About C-COM Satellite Systems Inc.

C-COM Satellite Systems Inc. is a pioneer and a leading global designer, developer, and manufacturer of transportable and mobile satellite-based antenna systems. The Company has developed proprietary, auto-acquisition controller technology for rapid antenna pointing to a satellite with just the press of a button, enabling Broadband Internet via Satellite across a wide range of market applications worldwide, including regions unserved or underserved by terrestrial access technologies.

C-COM has sold more than 11,000 antenna systems, in over 100 countries, through a dedicated dealer network that provides service to a wide range of vertical markets such as Oil and Gas Exploration, Military Communications, Disaster Management, SNG, Emergency Communications, Cellular Backhaul, Telemedicine, Mobile Education, Government Services, Mobile Banking, and others. The Company's iNetVu® brand is synonymous with high quality, reliability, and cost-effectiveness.

C-COM is in the final stages of satellite testing and manufacturing of a Ka-band, electronically steerable, modular, conformal, flat panel phased array antenna. The Company developed this multi-orbit antenna to provide low-cost, high-throughput mobility applications over satellite for land, airborne and maritime verticals across LEO, MEO and GEO satellite constellations. C-COM believes this technology has the potential to significantly expand its addressable markets across land mobility, maritime and airborne communications.

C-COM is developing an 8-channel Ka-band Analog Beamforming Integrated Circuit (BFIC), which is now in the manufacturing phase. These proprietary BFICs are intended to serve as a core building block of C-COM's next-generation antenna technology and will be integrated across the Company's entire Electronically Steerable Array (ESA) antenna product line. This integration is expected to significantly reduce manufacturing costs while enhancing antenna performance, giving C-COM an important competitive advantage in the evolving ESA market.
